frf.text: Yasova Dragonclaw is the Temur khan Sarkhan meets after he arrives in Tarkir's past, when her sabertooth pins him in the snow and she demands a reason to spare him. Yasova believes the dragons fall if Ugin dies, and she tells Sarkhan that a great golden dragon appeared in her vision and asked her to chart the storms so that he could find and kill Ugin.
Sarkhan realizes that her voice is Bolas and flees as a dragon to protect Ugin, but Yasova's spell grips him and Ugin is mortally wounded.

Later Yasova confesses to the other khans that she helped a malevolent dragon spirit attack Ugin in hopes of ending the storms, and Reyhan blames her for the deaths of thousands, though the khans forgive her. After Reyhan is killed by Silumgar, she leads her warriors to Ayagor and feeds a mammoth to Atarka as a gift, asking to stop fighting and saying that the future is not yet written.

dtk.text: Yasova cuts a claw-rune pathway that tracks the tempests, which Sarkhan sees was meant to be seen from the air by Nicol Bolas. Her elemental spell strikes dozens of dragons, including Sarkhan, and drowns out Ugin's call so the dragons converge on Ugin instead of Bolas.

Her sabertooth digs Sarkhan out and Yasova begins healing him, but when she tries to stop him from saving Ugin he blasts her with dragon fire. Sarkhan then defies her, wraps Ugin in a hedron cocoon, and is whisked back to an altered present, where Yasova's feeding of mammoth carcasses to Atarka keeps the Temur from attack.

bbd.text: Years later Yasova Dragonclaw, now the grandmother of the twins Baishya and Naiva, is a hunter band's leader whose banned name, Dragonclaw, Atarka has punished with death, and Ugin calls her to come to him. When Atarka's broodlings demand the clan's shamans, she lies about where the camp stood and distracts them with goblin corpses.

On the way to Ugin's grave she avoids an Ojutai dragon, and although she suspects a trap by Ojutai's broodling, Naiva and Baishya insist that she heal the wounded Tae Jin, which she does. He explains his master's dream, and an Ojutai broodling soon appears to sentence him to die by ice.

m19.text: As the Ojutai broodling prepares to kill Tae Jin, Yasova secretly signals the hunters to kill, and she and Naiva spear its aven interpreter. She decides to go on to Ugin's grave and asks Tae Jin to tell more about Ugin and Bolas, though she then demands the truth when she identifies his mark as that of a ghostfire warrior.

When Tae Jin finishes his story, Yasova says she witnessed Ugin's death eighteen years ago and reveals that Bolas killed Ugin and that she was used as a tool. When Atarka arrives and finds her dead broodling, Yasova claims Tae Jin has come to serve Atarka and stops him from raising his ghostfire blade.

She leads the twins to a hidden sanctuary and tells them they must become guardians of the carved memories of the ancestors, then crawls into the hedron to reach Ugin through Baishya. When Bolas threatens to destroy Tarkir unless she is brought to him, and Naiva, her mind twisted by him, holds a knife to Baishya's throat, Yasova disarms her and confesses she helped Bolas track Ugin because he promised her an end to dragons.

Yasova gambles by surrendering herself to Bolas and tells him that the Immortal Sun is pointed at this very spot, so that he strikes the canyon and flees, leaving her and Baishya alive. She closes by telling the girls that even the greatest of dragons can die and that anything may come to pass in the unwritten now.
